title: Module quiz: Claude Code for developers

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A new repository has no memory file, and a developer needs a useful one by the end of the day. Which sequence fits?

options.text: Pull in a very large template with imports, then keep the main file short
options.says: Ruled out because imports "don't reduce its context cost, because imported files also load at launch".

options.text: Write every convention by hand, then run `/compact` on that file
options.says: Ruled out because `/compact` is for the conversation: "use `/context` to see what fills the window and `/compact` to summarise it".

options.text: Run `/init`, then add every convention the team has ever used
options.says: Ruled out because "Longer files consume more context and reduce adherence", so adding everything works against the file.

options.text: Run `/init`, then delete lines Claude would have found anyway
options.says: The page says `/init` "analyzes your codebase and creates a file with build commands, test instructions, and project conventions it discovers", then to "cut what Claude would have found anyway".

questions.stem: A nightly script runs `claude -p` and sometimes loops on tool calls for an hour. Which pair of flags bounds it?

options.text: A turn limit and a spend cap on the run
options.says: The page says "`--max-turns` limits the number of agentic turns, and `--max-budget-usd` caps the spend."

options.text: A permission mode and a tool list for the run
options.says: Ruled out because "`--permission-mode dontAsk` runs reads and pre-approved tools", which decides what may run and not how long.

options.text: A bare switch and a JSON output format on the run
options.says: Ruled out because "Use `json` when a script parses the result", and bare mode only skips discovery, so neither bounds a loop.

options.text: A resume flag and a fork flag for the next run
options.says: Ruled out because `--resume` reopens a session "under the same session ID and appends new messages to the existing conversation", which continues a loop and does not bound it.

questions.stem: A team wants the review script to inspect code and change nothing, with no prompt ever shown. Which setup fits?

options.text: `bypassPermissions`, with the runner as the only boundary
options.says: Ruled out because `bypassPermissions` is for "Isolated containers and VMs only", and it runs everything.

options.text: `auto`, with the classifier left to judge every single call
options.says: Ruled out because auto mode "reviews actions instead of you" and runs most calls, not reads alone.

options.text: `dontAsk`, with `Read` and read-only git patterns listed
options.says: The page says `--permission-mode dontAsk` "runs reads and pre-approved tools and denies anything that would prompt, which fits a script", with `Read` and read-only git patterns.

options.text: `acceptEdits`, with edits approved for the whole checkout
options.says: Ruled out because `acceptEdits` runs "Reads, file edits, and common filesystem commands", which is more than reads.

questions.stem: A developer in Manual mode is tired of approving each source change, but wants a prompt before every other action. Which mode fits?

options.text: `plan`, which makes no edits until a plan is approved
options.says: Ruled out because plan mode is where "Claude reads files and proposes a plan but makes no edits until you approve", so changes wait for approval.

options.text: `acceptEdits`, which lets edits and filesystem commands run
options.says: The table gives `acceptEdits` "Reads, file edits, and common filesystem commands", and other shell commands still ask.

options.text: `dontAsk`, which denies each action that would prompt
options.says: Ruled out because `dontAsk` "runs reads and pre-approved tools and denies anything that would prompt", so nothing asks.

options.text: `auto`, where a second model reviews the actions instead
options.says: Ruled out because auto mode runs "Everything, with background safety checks", so shell work does not prompt either.
